description: Single-panel line schematic (no micrograph, no data curve) drawn on a grey, slightly skewed rectangular specimen outline labelled "SPCE" in the top-right corner, with "Unit: µm" printed at the bottom right. A horizontal reference line runs across the specimen and carries four diamond-shaped symbols in a row — the Vickers indentation marks used for position identification. Dimension chains between neighbouring marks read 300, 340 and 300 from left to right (unit µm). At the top left a dimension of 1150 is drawn from the left specimen edge to a vertical extension line that drops toward the marker row; the left-hand vertical dimension 2660 spans from the top edge down to the horizontal marker line, giving the marker line's depth from the top edge. Two leader-labelled annotations, "Marker for finding me" and "Marker for finding location", point to the two interior markers. No scale bar is present — all sizes are given numerically. Taken together the panel documents the marker layout that lets a targeted grain boundary be relocated after CMP: outer markers find the indentation region, inner ones fix the exact measurement point. The text states the outer markers are larger, but the four diamonds look nearly equal at the supplied resolution.
measured_quantities: marker spacing between adjacent indentation marks (µm)
distance from specimen left edge to marker row (µm)
distance from specimen top edge to marker line (µm)

observations.observation: The figure is a schematic drawing of a single specimen plate labelled "SPCE" in the top-right corner, with "Unit: µm" printed at bottom right.
Four diamond-shaped markers (Vickers indentation marks) lie in a row on one horizontal reference line across the specimen.
Dimensions printed between neighbouring markers are 300, 340 and 300 (µm) from left to right along the marker row.

A horizontal dimension of 1150 (µm) is drawn at the top from the left specimen edge to a vertical extension line, and a vertical dimension of 2660 (µm) at the left runs from the top edge to the marker line.
Two leader-labelled annotations, "Marker for finding me" and "Marker for finding location", point down to the two interior markers of the row.
The figure's metadata states it shows the location of the markers for position identification.

The citing text states that the larger markers at the outer side are used for finding the region for indentation and the smaller ones inside are used for deciding the exact position of the measurement point.

The citing text states the specimen surfaces were treated with an etching solution, the targeted grain boundary was measured under the microscope, two indentation marks were made near the boundary with a Vickers hardness test machine, and CMP was then applied to the surface finish.
At the supplied resolution the four diamond markers appear nearly equal in size, so the outer-larger / inner-smaller distinction asserted in the text is not clearly confirmed by the pixels.
No indentation hardness values, elastic-modulus values or grain-boundary misorientation angles are printed anywhere in the panel; only positional dimensions in µm appear.

unreadable_items: Exact alignment of the 1150 µm extension line with a specific marker is ambiguous at the supplied resolution
Size difference between the outer and inner markers (stated in the citing text) cannot be resolved in the drawing
Small annotation text near the leaders is only partially readable; "Marker for finding me" may be a truncated/OCR-affected label
